etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English unpakken, equivalent to un- +‎ pack. Compare Saterland Frisian uutpakje (“to unpack”), West Frisian útpakke (“to unpack”), Dutch uitpakken (“to unpack”), German auspacken (“to unpack”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To remove from a package or container, particularly with respect to items that had previously been arranged closely and securely in a pack.
(intransitive) To empty containers that had been packed.
(figurative, transitive) To analyze a concept or a text; to explain.

quote.citation: 2013 September 20, Anne Enright, “A Girl Is a Half-Formed Thing by Eimear McBride – review”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: There may be another argument here, if we had time to unpack it, about modernism and the rise of the middle classes.

quote.citation: 2019 October 17, Steven Rattner, “Unpacking the Trade Deficit”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: Yet few Americans — including the president — understand how global trade works, both how it can help our economy and how some can be left behind. Let’s try to unpack a few of the complexities.

quote.citation: 2021 March 8, Helen Sullivan, “Meghan and Harry: 12 things we learned from the Oprah special”, in The Guardian‎[3]:
quote.text: From a gender reveal to a secret ceremony and rifts with other royal family members, there was a lot to unpack from the interview

definitions.definition: (linguistics, intransitive, of a segment such as a vowel) To undergo separation of its features into distinct segments.

quote.text: The rounded vowels [y] and [œ/ə] in Russian seem to unpack as glide-vowel sequences in words borrowed from French and German,  […]

quote.citation: 2008, Katrin Dohlus, The Role of Phonology and Phonetics in Loanword Adaptation, page 73:
quote.text: Whereas the high vowels /ʏ, y/ unpack, the mid vowels /œ, ø/ are adapted as single segments in these languages (see examples in (36) for Vietnamese (Barker 1969) and (37) for Fon (Gbeto 2000)).  […] French /y/ → Vietnamese /wi/accu [a'ky] → ac-quy [ak kwi]

quote.citation: 2011, John A. Goldsmith, Jason Riggle, Alan C. L. Yu, editors, The Handbook of Phonological Theory:
quote.text: The objective of these corpora was to check whether vowels other than nasal vowels systematically unpack in L1s that do not allow them.
